layout: offset 0..11  position x,y,z    float32 x3, little-endian
offset 12..23 scale    sx,sy,sz float32 x3, already exp()-decoded
offset 28..31 quat     w,x,y,z  uint8 x4, q*128+128
The 32 bytes ARE the two RGBA32UI texels the renderer uploads: texels[0] = (x,y,z,sx),
texels[1] = (sy,sz,colourWord,quatWord), each word the little-endian uint32 at its offset.

recordsList.name: first
recordsList.why: the file’s first record: an ordinary splat whose baked opacity (alpha 43) makes the quad SHRINK — Splat.extentScaleForAlpha gives sqrt(2 ln(43)) / 3 = 0.914 — and whose quaternion is far from identity, so the q*128+128 decode and the R S S^T R^T rotation are both exercised

recordsList.name: bright
recordsList.why: THE record this contract exists for: an opaque bright splat whose colour word reads as a float32 NaN. Uploaded as RGBA32F (the prototype’s path) the colour comes back through floatBitsToUint as a canonical NaN on Mali and this splat draws flat white; uploaded as RGBA32UI the bytes ARE the texel. The exact condition is the exponent: ((alpha & 0x7F) << 1) | (blue >> 7) == 0xFF, i.e. alpha 127 or 255 and blue >= 128

recordsList.name: opaque
recordsList.why: a fully opaque, mid-file record: the alpha-extent clip is the IDENTITY here (sqrt(2 ln 255) = 3.33 > 3, so the whole 3-sigma quad is kept), which is the other end of the range from `first`

recordsList.name: padding
recordsList.why: the node pads a budget out with zero records, and a real cloud therefore ENDS in them: 32 zero bytes must decode without throwing and must be culled (`z > 0` is the shader’s test), not divided by
